reference_answer:
Assume UpperPrefix(A,k): for every earlier column c<k, A[r,c]=0 whenever c<r. This is a STRICT-below-diagonal condition, not a claim that A[c,c]=0. For exampleI_2 has UpperPrefix at k=1 while A[0,0]=1; a proof demanding that diagonal zero would be false.

For k<M and k<N, the actual sweep acts only on the row window k,...,N-1, bottom-up. Fresh column k is zero at every row r>k after columnSweep_zeroed. For an old column c<k, EVERY row r in the swept window satisfies r>=k>c. Consequently all entries of old column c in that window are zero by the prefix hypothesis. Each two-row rotation combines two zero entries of that old column into two zeros, while rows outside the window are unchanged. Equivalently columnSweep_preserves_zero_column applies with lo=k and count=N-1-k. Thus old entries retain their previous values everywhere and in particular retain their required below-diagonal zeros; the old diagonal row c is outside the swept window and need not be zero. Combining old columns with fresh column k gives UpperPrefix at k+1.

If k>=N, no pivot row exists and the actual procedure skips the sweep. Every old c<k remains covered. The only newly included column c=k has no row r>k in Fin N, so its required clause is vacuous. Hence the same one-index advance holds without a hidden k<N assumption on all processed columns.

Now induct on the number of remaining columns, starting with the vacuous UpperPrefix(A,0). Each processed or skipped column advances the index by one. After M columns UpperPrefix(reduced(A),M) holds. For any actual column c in Fin M, c<M; if c<r, the invariant gives reduced(A)[r,c]=0. This is the claimed upper-trapezoidal residual. N=0 or M=0 is harmless: there are no rows/columns witnessing a forbidden entry and the empty/skipping recursions preserve the vacuous invariant. No nonzero pivot, full rank, diagonal normalization, cost or numerical stability premise was needed.

rubric.criterion: Show the freshly swept column is zero below its diagonal
Show earlier columns' below-diagonal zeros are preserved by the new sweep
Induct from the vacuous index 0 to full upper-trapezoidal residual at index M

exposition.core_summary: The strict upper-prefix invariant survives because the next sweep touches rows r>=k, all strictly below every earlier column c<k. No old diagonal entry is assumed zero; skipped pivots and empty dimensions are vacuous.

semantic_steps.claim: For an existing pivot k<N, the actual bottom-up sweep zeros fresh column k only strictly below its diagonal.
Earlier c<k has zero entries throughout the later swept window r>=k>c; zero-column preservation and unchanged outside rows retain the old invariant without zeroing A[c,c].
Fresh zeroing and old-column preservation give UpperPrefix(k+1); when k>=N the fresh clause is vacuous and the skipped sweep also advances it.
Induction from the vacuous index0 gives UpperPrefix(M), hence all entries with c<r vanish, including empty row/column boundaries.
